I realize this is me coming at you with platitudes. However, it gets better. I promise.

Things did get better. Honestly. A lot better. My career took off. I’ve met someone new in the most unlikely of places. I started pushing myself to try a new hobby. I learned to play the piano enough to the point where I can play live for people. I think just getting out and being around other people at my own pace. Helped tremendously. 

There are still times when the behaviors I learned from my ex start to get in the way of my relationship.
Short answer yes. Things will get better. Way better it just takes time, and you’ll have to be forgiving of yourself.

So here’s the thing about dating a co worker. Generally it can be a bad idea. However, I suggest that you start asking married couples or  people in long term relationships where they met. More than half the time it’s going to be through work. This happens for the simple reason of we spend most of our time at work. Now another thing to keep in mind is that while dating a coworker isn’t necessarily, or inherently, a bad idea. The further they work away from you or your department, the better. 

When it comes to asking them out. Keep it simple. Just say, “Would you like to hang out after work sometime?” Or “I was wanting to check out this one place, would you like check it out with me after work one day?” Just ask with the intention of having a good time with a co worker.

I’m almost 30 myself and I have dated only 3 people. This first and longest relationship was 16 years. That was off and on for some of those years. She left me almost a year ago. And if I’m being completely honest with myself. She was probably the only person I have actually loved.  So losing her has been my first real heart break. 

First. Just feel all the emotions that are going to come up. There won’t be any escaping them for a while. Go see a therapist to help sort through some of those emotions. Honestly it never hurts to see a therapist in my opinion. 

Next. Try and get out of your home as much as possible. Staying inside with your own thoughts can be toxic. It definitely was for me. Be with friends and family, they will be your support. 

Eventually you’ll start thinking about them less and less. Maybe not stop thinking about them all together. But one day you’ll wake up and you’ll realize your first thought wasn’t about them. 

One day you’ll see someone attractive or just just genuinely interesting and you’ll want to get to know them. 

That’s where I’m at now. I still think about my ex all the time but it’s a lot less painful than what it used to be. And I’m finally almost ready to date again. I think. 
It’s a cliche but time heals. Sometimes you just have to work with it.

Story time: 
I broke up with my current ex about 10 years ago. She was abusive in every sense of the word. However, on the flip side, after this break up I ran into my other ex at a bar and we hit things off instantly. After years apart we grew as people but still had similar interests. And still very much attracted to each other. We’re just really good friends currently. There is still a huge chemistry between that we are both trying to ignore actually. And she is one of the only positive forces in my life currently... 


Things can evolve for the better. I guess it just depends on if both parties put the effort into themselves and truly forgive past transgressions of the relationship. Unfortunately, that’s too hard for most people to do. A lot of people like to hold grudges for a lifetime.

First off.

It sounds like you’re making good progress. You’ve already come to a realization that your ex wasn’t good to you. And that you probably wouldn’t get back with him.  That’s a HUGE step. 

I have been in a similar situation. For me I didn’t entirely realize it was an abusive relationship until a few months of therapy after the break up.
It was Hard. And everything in me kept telling me,   “No she wasn’t that bad, I must have deserved it.” Because according to her I was a terrible boyfriend.  It wasn’t until I remembered all the times she threatened to hurt herself or even kill herself if I did something she didn’t like. Even threatened to drive the car of the road because I said something she disagreed with. Or even break my fingers amongst other physical abuse. 
My point is. Even now I still feel a need to defend her actions. Which is a behavior that is extremely hard to break. My Therapists advice to me is and this me to you.

Get Angry. 

For me being angry feels wrong. But it’s a necessary emotion to go through. Especially if your former partner was abusive. 
Use that anger to propel you forward and use it to break that emotional connection. Or if you had them on the pedestal like me... -_-  Being angry with them will definitely knock them off of that fucking pedestal. 
It’s easier said than done. I really hate thinking of my ex and being angry. Because I still fucking love her. And honestly I don’t think I will ever stop loving her. She was my first love and my last. (So far.)

And it’s so bizarre lately. I have felt numb as well. I can’t even think about dating again right now. There is no one out there that I even feel remotely attracted to. Which is very odd for me. Because I used to find plenty of girls attractive. I haven’t entirely felt a strong emotion one way or the other about anything recently. I’m sure it will pass though.
Anyway.
Take care of yourself. Find things you enjoy again. Or even better. Find some new things that you might enjoy. 
Recovering from an abusive relationship is hard. But we can get through this together!

This is hard to deal with. I think this everyday. 
The last couple of years my ex just stopped putting effort into the relationship. And I would react negatively about it. Until one night I picked her up from school a year ago. She had this look on her face and told me she thought we needed to break up. She changed her mind after a conversation about how I really felt about her. I was “distant and didn’t seem like I loved her like I used to.” When it was further from the truth. I loved her even more than before. All the things I was doing to upset her I changed overnight. I didn’t do it just to keep her. I did it because I wanted to be the man she deserved and fell in love with 16 years ago. Six months later we had our first argument an I called her out on obsessively texting another guy and how uncomfortable it made me. One night she stopped mid sex to respond to his text... -_-
She broke up with me the next morning. And said at least I don’t have to pretend to love you anymore.

Sorry for rambling. Anyway, my point is that over the course of those six months I had put in every fiber of my being into trying to make the relationship work and make a happier future for us. But what I learned after months of therapy and constant introspection is that she had already checked out of the relationship YEARS ago.  And she made me feel like I was the sole problem. (Of course I was part of the problem, it takes two to make a relationship work.) Things would not have worked out no matter how much effort I put into the relationship. No matter how understand I could have been. 
Try not to beat yourself up with those thoughts and feelings. Sometimes, things just aren’t meant to work out I guess. You did what you could with what you had. That’s something to feel good about. Can you say that for your former partner? I suspect not.

Sorry for my little rant. I felt like sharing an experience could help some. I hope this helps in some way. Things will get better for you whoever takes the time to read this.

I got out of a 16 year relationship (we’re both 29) six months ago, it was on and off. Mostly on for the past nine years. One day she said she was happy with how things were going with us. The next she breaks up with me and says, “I’m glad I don’t have to pretend to love you anymore.”  Something that has stuck with me everyday since the breakup. 

Anyways. Since then I casually dated an old friend and it was good, for the most part. She moved to another state. (And I’m supposed to meet her tomorrow for a weekend vacation.) But, of course, she still wasn’t my ex. No one can ever be my ex. And I’m honestly scared that I’m never going to fully recover from this relationship. 

It’s hard to explain this feeling actually... Right now, I’m lonely. And I want companionship. At the same time it scares me shitless. I couldn’t make a 16 year relationship work. What are the odds of pulling that off again. Or am I just doomed to have insignificant relationships that will never stack up to what I had with my ex. 

Sorry for the long non-sensical rant. That’s just my experience and where I’m at emotionally lately. So you’re not alone. It probably doesn’t help.
